newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank governor sees high Thai interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank governor sees high Thai interest rates.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Thursday a bullish U.S. dollar and speculation on the currency will likely keep short-term Thai interest rates at relatively high levels in the near term.

"There is a clear sign that the dollar will continue its upward trend. Investor speculation in the dollar will cause the short-term interest rates to remain high during this period," Rerngchai told reporters.
Rerngchai said high short-term interest rates this week could also be attributed to heavy seasonal demand for funds during the Lunar New Year holiday.
The central bank has asked the state-owned Government Savings Bank to help inject funds into the market to help ease tight liquidity, the governor told reporters.

The overnight interbank rate was quoted at a six-month high of 18.00-20.00 percent by midday on Thursday. Dealers said the liquidity squeeze was compounded by a requirement for commercial banks to build their reserves by Friday.
"The central bank still maintains the repurchase interest rates at high levels because we don't want banks to use funds for speculating in foreign exchange markets," he said.
The repurchase rates are what the central bank charges commercial banks for funds extended through the Bank of Thailand's bond repurchase window.
The central bank raised its one-day bond repurchase rate to 18.00 percent on Thursday morning from 16.00 late on Wednesday.

Rerngchai said although the central bank still sticks to its policy of defending the baht by intervening in local and offshore markets, the BOT has not intervened in these markets since late last week.
The baht was traded at 25.98/25.99 to the dollar at midday, sharply lower than the central bank's midrate fixing of 25.90.
Dealers said recent heavy dollar buying was triggered by the strength of the U.S. unit in major markets and concerns about the weak Thai stock market.
